summary: Derived two bounded candidates pending distinct review. First, the moving unit operator is an orthogonal compression of a coefficient-one operator enlarged to all primitive image states, with unchanged original prime groups and weights. Finite singular-value contraction gives the true trace-power inequality; endpoint root moments cost the explicit maximum weighted list-fiber norm, whose 1/(2R)-root is harmless at the stated source J,R scales. An ambient-power restricted endpoint Gram bound supplies an alternative finite pairing route. An explicit matrix refutes pointwise deletion of intermediate projections, and source endpoint moments do not automatically control an enlarged trace. Second, proved an exact bijection of enlarged roots with unit-r triples vr=-H mod u, including multiple sector preimages, and the joint projective-line/ratio count with main density 1/(zeta(2)*prod(p+1)) and error O_eta((sigma_-3/4(H)*U^(7/4+eta)+V)*log²(2U)). Every squarefree S is supported, including primes dividing H. All zero modes, nonunit-H gcd costs, prime powers and R-exclusion costs are retained. Power saving is restricted to b>3a/4; balanced boxes give exponent1/8. Relative heights and boundary derivatives have 1+UV/H control. Pinned Guo source already contains enlarged-state and restricted-Gram framing; its H2'-conditional transport is not validated. No full trace/path estimate, actual-prime cancellation, source extension, Goldbach proof, breakthrough or novelty is obtained. Usage is unknown.

claims.text: The finite unit-sector operator is an orthogonal compression of the specified enlarged operator, and its trace powers and endpoint root moments obey the displayed Schatten/frame bounds with the explicit list-fiber factor.
The assertion that intermediate projections may always be deleted with a pointwise upper inequality inside diagonal trace-power terms is refuted by the displayed matrix.
Enlarged roots are in bijection with the stated unit-r determinant-H triples, with the displayed multiplicity over a fixed original pair.
The enlarged joint root count has the displayed density and absolute error for every squarefree prescribed modulus, including primes dividing H, and gives the stated restricted-aspect power saving.
The real relative-coordinate heights and box-boundary derivatives have the stated 1+UV/H control, without establishing the accumulated path variation or moment estimate.
The required enlarged trace/path cancellation, changed prime major part, actual-prime correlation, source-theorem extension, novelty and Goldbach remain unestablished.
